properties.name: Flame extinction
properties.description: Termination of combustion under specified chemical and transport conditions.

properties.name: Microgravity combustion
properties.description: Combustion studied under reduced buoyancy in a microgravity environment.

properties.name: Flame oscillations
properties.description: Time-dependent oscillation of flame structure or burning behavior.

properties.name: Cool flames
properties.description: Low-temperature combustion associated with fuel oxidation chemistry.

properties.name: Spherical diffusion flames
properties.description: Non-premixed flames arranged approximately spherically around a source or sink.

properties.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
properties.summary: ACME CFI-G investigates gaseous-fuel cool diffusion flames in normal and inverse spherical configurations. The tables include ignition outcomes, burn duration, termination and burner-temperature observations, including unsuccessful ignition attempts. These outcomes are preserved separately from the project hypotheses about cool-flame stability and transitions.

properties.title: ACME CFI-G — investigation-level study
properties.summary: ACME CFI-G investigates gaseous-fuel cool diffusion flames in normal and inverse spherical configurations. The tables include ignition outcomes, burn duration, termination and burner-temperature observations, including unsuccessful ignition attempts. These outcomes are preserved separately from the project hypotheses about cool-flame stability and transitions.

conditions.scope: Study-level description; not a single physical test.
conditions.observations_vs_objectives: Metadata objectives and hypotheses are not treated as measured findings.

methods: Cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes and thermocouples

properties.summary: Normal and inverse ethane, propane and n-butane flames were investigated. The report says gaseous cool diffusion flames were obtained only for normal n-butane flames at 2 bar and ambient oxygen mole fraction 0.39 in this campaign. Hot precursor flames were reported as 2.6 times larger. A separate ground pool-flame study in the report is not classified as an ISS experiment. Ethane replaced the originally proposed n-pentane.

properties.title: CFI-G: observed gaseous cool diffusion flames
properties.summary: Normal and inverse ethane, propane and n-butane flames were investigated. The report says gaseous cool diffusion flames were obtained only for normal n-butane flames at 2 bar and ambient oxygen mole fraction 0.39 in this campaign. Hot precursor flames were reported as 2.6 times larger. A separate ground pool-flame study in the report is not classified as an ISS experiment. Ethane replaced the originally proposed n-pentane.

properties.title: Cool diffusion flames in a stably stratified stagnation flow

evidence.locator: metadata.objective
evidence.text: 1. Plan and support flight testing on the International Space Station (ISS). 2. Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames; and a broad range of Zst, Tad, and fluent flow rate. 3. Support the flight tests with advanced CFD simulations. 4. Identify or develop a chemical kinetics mechanism that yields good agreement between the CFD predictions and the ISS measurements. 5. Disseminate the results as widely as possible.

evidence.locator: metadata.approach
evidence.text: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests aboard the International Space Station. Consider multiple fuels, a range of reactant dilutions, flow rates, and pressures for normal and inverse convection directions. Observe the flames with a broad suite of cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, and thermocouples.

Consider multiple fuels, a range of reactant dilutions, flow rates, and pressures for normal and inverse convection directions. Observe the flames with a broad suite of cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, and thermocouples.

evidence.locator: metadata.objective
evidence.text: 1. Plan and support flight testing on the International Space Station (ISS). 2. Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames; and a broad range of Zst, Tad, and fluent flow rate. 3. Support the flight tests with advanced CFD simulations. 4. Identify or develop a chemical kinetics mechanism that yields good agreement between the CFD predictions and the ISS measurements. 5. Disseminate the results as widely as possible.
